valueObject.general: {subject} can only exist valid. Its constructor checks the constraints and answers with an error value instead of throwing, so once you hold one nobody needs to check it again.
valueObject.typescript: It is a branded type: the compiler will not mix it up with any other number or string, and `create` is the only door in.
valueObject.python: It subclasses `int` or `str`, so it behaves like the plain value, and `create` answers with `Ok` or `Err`.
valueObject.ruby: It is a module with `create` and `trusted`; the value stays a plain Integer or String, checked when it enters the domain.
valueObject.ruby-dry: `Type` is the dry-types base used by the structs, and `create` answers with `Success` or `Failure` from dry-monads.

entity.general: {subject} has an identity: two lines with the same data are different lines if their ids differ. Values that follow from its data, like a subtotal, live next to it.
entity.typescript: A class with `readonly` fields; derived values are getters.
entity.python: A frozen dataclass; derived values are properties.
entity.ruby: A Struct with keyword arguments; derived values are plain methods.
entity.ruby-dry: A `Dry::Struct`: typed attributes, immutable once built.

aggregateOutline.general: Before any code, this is the shape of {subject}: the states it passes through, what moves it, what it checks first and what it announces. The rules that always hold sit on top.

aggregateCode.general: {subject} is the only way in. Its state is private and a command never changes it in place: it answers with the new aggregate and the events, or with the reason it refused.
aggregateCode.typescript: The state sits in a private `state` object, and every command ends in `transition`, which also checks the invariants.
aggregateCode.python: The state lives in `_state`, and every command returns `Ok` or `Err` through `_transition`.
aggregateCode.ruby: The state lives in a private Struct, and commands answer with `Result.ok` or `Result.err` through `transition`.
aggregateCode.ruby-dry: The state is a private `Dry::Struct`, and commands answer with `Success` or `Failure` through `transition`.

invariant.general: Guards run before a transition and invariants run on its result, every time. Break one and the aggregate answers with an error code instead of changing. Pick an attack above and watch the lines that stop it.
invariant.typescript: A refusal is a value: `return err({ code: "…" })`. Nothing is thrown.
invariant.python: A refusal is a value: `return err(…Error(code="…"))`. Nothing is raised.
invariant.ruby: A refusal is a value: `return reject(:code) if …`. Nothing is raised.
invariant.ruby-dry: A refusal is a value: `return reject(:code) if …`, which is a `Failure`. Nothing is raised.

event.general: {subject} is a fact in the past. It carries only what others need to react, and the aggregate hands it back when the transition succeeds.
event.typescript: An interface with readonly fields and a `type` tag, so a list of events is a discriminated union.
event.python: A frozen dataclass with a `type` class variable.
event.ruby-dry: A `Dry::Struct` with typed attributes and a `type` method.

repository.general: The domain only says what it needs from storage, find and save, and leaves how to someone else. That is what lets you change the database without touching a single rule.
repository.typescript: An `interface`: the compiler holds every implementation to it.
repository.python: A `Protocol`: any class with those methods qualifies.
repository.ruby: A documented contract: Ruby relies on duck typing, so the module only states it.
repository.ruby-dry: A documented contract: Ruby relies on duck typing, so the module only states it.

factory.general: {subject} is born in a valid initial state. `start` asks only for what it cannot live without and sets the rest to its starting value, so nobody else needs to know how to build one.
factory.ruby: A class method `start` with keyword arguments, so a call reads like a sentence.
factory.ruby-dry: A class method `start` with keyword arguments; the state it builds is checked by Dry::Struct.

domainService.general: When a rule involves several aggregates and does not belong to any of them, it gets a domain service: a plain operation named in the business language, with no state of its own.

applicationService.general: The use case in four moves: load the aggregate, give it the command, save what comes back and publish its events. It holds no rules; the aggregate does.

constrainedTypes.general: {subject} is not a bare string or number: it is a type that only admits legal values. The check happens once, where the value is built, and every function after that can trust it.

statesAsTypes.general: Each step of the process has its own type, and the highlighted fields are what that step adds. An order that is not paid yet is a different thing from one that is, and the code says so.

illegalStates.general: Make the illegal state impossible to write. A function that charges a payment only accepts a priced checkout, so charging a checkout nobody validated is not a bug to test for: it does not compile.

pipeline.general: A business process as an assembly line: every stage takes the type the previous one produced and returns the next. Reading the stages in order reads the process.

errorsAsValues.general: Expected failures, such as a declined card, are not exceptions: they are values returned on a second track. Break a stage and see that nothing after it runs and nothing is thrown.

newNotes.general: The wall grows: the highlighted notes are what the change needs, new events, commands and states. Nothing that was already there had to be thrown away.

evolutionDiff.general: Only the lines that follow from the change are new; everything else stays as it was. That is what a model that speaks the language of the business buys you.

breakthrough.general: Back to the whole wall, now in version 2. Sometimes a change reveals a concept that makes many things simpler at once. That is a breakthrough, and it is worth the refactor.

layers.general: A layered architecture looks tidy, but its dependencies run downwards, all the way to the infrastructure. The most valuable code ends up depending on the least stable.

hexagonal.general: Turn it inside out: the domain is at the centre and defines what it needs as ports. Everything else, screens, databases, gateways, plugs in from the outside.

portsAdapters.general: A port is an interface the domain owns; an adapter is the outside code that implements it. Replace a SQL database with one in memory and not a line of the domain changes.

dependencyRule.general: Source code dependencies point only inwards. Adapters know the domain; the domain knows nothing of adapters. That one rule is what keeps the centre free.

statesAsTypesCode.general: Each type here is the data at one step of the process: a priced checkout has everything a validated one has, plus its total. Nothing optional, nothing half-filled.
statesAsTypesCode.typescript: Plain interfaces with readonly fields. The compiler refuses a ValidatedCheckout where a PricedCheckout is needed.
statesAsTypesCode.python: Frozen dataclasses, one per step, built only by the stage before.
statesAsTypesCode.ruby: Structs with keyword arguments, one per step. Ruby will not stop you passing the wrong one, so the order of the stages and the tests carry that guarantee.
statesAsTypesCode.ruby-dry: Dry::Struct classes: the typed attributes are checked when an instance is built, so a wrong shape fails right there.

pipelineCode.general: The pipeline only wires the stages in order. Each line calls a stage with what the previous one returned and stops at the first failure. The ports are what the outside world provides.
pipelineCode.typescript: `checkoutWorkflow(ports)` returns the function that runs the pipeline.
pipelineCode.python: The function returns `run`, which holds the ports it was given.
pipelineCode.ruby: A class that receives the ports and runs the pipeline with `call`.
pipelineCode.ruby-dry: A class that receives the ports and runs the pipeline with `call`, answering with Success or Failure.

errorsAsValuesCode.general: This stage never raises. When the port refuses, it returns that failure as a value and the pipeline passes it on, so the caller always gets an answer it can inspect.

adapterCode.general: The adapter lives outside the domain and implements the repository port. This one keeps aggregates in memory: perfect for tests, and the domain cannot tell the difference.
adapterCode.typescript: A class that `implements` the port, so the compiler checks every method against it.
adapterCode.python: A plain class with the same methods as the Protocol: Python checks the shape, not the name.
adapterCode.ruby: A plain class with `find` and `save`: duck typing is the only contract.
adapterCode.ruby-dry: A plain class with `find` and `save`: duck typing is the only contract.
